scope: Fresh full v2 API policy comparison with an explicit 30000-ms initial navigation cap on both profiles. One primary and two alternate owners, four global HTTP workers/two per policy. Not a matched code-version or equal-resource comparison with the previous 55/100 uncapped fork run or source-pinned 54/100 versus 81/100 actual hosted comparison. No hosted calls.

protocol.resourceDifference: One 2-CPU/2.5-GiB primary with two page slots and two 2-CPU/2-GiB alternates with one page slot each; 6.5-GiB aggregate browser memory in a 7.75-GiB Docker VM. Adaptive requests may use a second sequential browser attempt. Different topology/memory from previous runs; no equal-resource speed claim.

backendDispatchLedger.source: Original request URLs in retained browser-owner logs. This includes API errors with no returned fallback diagnostics.

realBrowserApiHarness.scope: Real API/queue/worker path with native Chromium and Linux Firefox owners against local HTTP fixtures. Includes typed navigation timeout recovery, preserved post-commit readiness, invalid control rejection and retained-session continuation/close.

limits: One fresh round does not establish stable per-target or WAF-brand success rates. Labels are from the frozen publisher fixture, not proof of active commercial WAF rules.
Normalized marker retrieval does not measure CSS visibility, extraction F1, complete crawling or recurring refresh.
Additional owner capacity, sequential attempts, live-site variation and socket throttling can affect latency. No equal-resource or causal browser-effect claim.
Returned recovery metadata is not identical to frozen-marker success. Missing diagnostics on API errors remain unknown; backend logs account for actual dispatches.
Hosted comparison remains source-pinned to the earlier deployment; no current hosted parity is inferred.

unmatchedPrecedingDeploymentComparison.scope: Unmatched preceding deployment and current explicit navigation-cap policy; same topology/page/memory limits and client concurrency, but source, request controls, live timing and browser identities differ. No causal aggregate speed claim.
